answers.question: What is S-NODE's answer: exact minimum Node version with node:sqlite and timeout and no flag?
answers.answer: Not answered yet. ADR-0002 explicitly says the minimum was not checked: 'Not checked: Node 22'. TECH-SPEC §9 lists S-NODE as an open spike, not a decided value. No number exists in any doc.

docGapFinding.gap: No minimum Node version is recorded; only 'Node 22: not checked' is noted in ADR-0002.

answers.recommendation: Run the spike: open node:sqlite with {timeout} on Node 22, 23, 24 LTS candidates and confirm busy_timeout actually takes effect (see WAL answer below — the option alone is not enough). Record the first version where this works with no --experimental flag.

answers.question: What is the exact ctx_resume compaction format inside the 2 KB cap: which fields, in what order?
answers.answer: ADR-0009 §5 Render gives the exact format: a single block `<context_mode_state session="ID" upto="MAXSEQ">`, then sections in a fixed order (last request, open errors, changed files, earlier requests, indexed sources), lines within each section in seq order, ending with `more: ctx_search(queries:[…], scope:"session")`, then the closing tag. Pointer lines for items over 640 B use the form `#<seq> (<bytes> B) ctx_resume(seq:<seq>)`. Budget is 2,048 UTF-8 bytes total (§4). GP6 golden-tests this exact byte-for-byte output for a 10,000-row journal.

answers.question: Is the single context.db per project locked with WAL mode, and what happens on GP8's '0 busy errors' when 4 servers write at once?
answers.answer: ADR-0002 decision #2 sets node:sqlite with {timeout: 5000}, BEGIN IMMEDIATE on every write, 1 MB index chunks, and explicitly 'No retry loop'. The measured '0 busy errors' result (8 writers, 4 FTS readers, 20 MB indexer) came from v1's spike, not yet v2 code. WAL mode itself is assumed (ADR-0001 in v1 history, lines 70-73/115-116) but is not re-stated as a v2 decision in ADR-0002.

archaeology.introducedBy: commit 302bb7b (#228, node:sqlite adapter), regressed again and refixed in commit 7afa0f45 (closes #642, Tue May 19 2026)
archaeology.originalIntent: "Restores the ADR-0001 multi-writer contract (WAL + busy_timeout + withRetry), which line 70-73 + 115-116 of the ADR explicitly assume holds on every driver."
archaeology.regressionRisk: BLOCKER: node:sqlite's DatabaseSync constructor silently ignores the {timeout} option — unlike better-sqlite3's native constructor. v1 shipped this exact bug (#642): passing {timeout: N} alone left busy_timeout at SQLite's default of 0, so the first write contention threw 'database is locked' immediately instead of waiting. ADR-0002's v2 decision text only says 'Engine: node:sqlite with {timeout: 5000}' and 'No retry loop' — it does not call out that {timeout} must be followed by an explicit `adapter.pragma(\`busy_timeout = ${opts.timeout}\`)` call, which is the one-line fix #642 actually needed. If M0's db layer trusts the constructor option the way v1 originally did, GP8's '0 busy errors' target will fail exactly the same way #642 failed in production (reporter: Aleksandr Yeganov, roughly 1 in 5 fresh sessions).
archaeology.safeFixConstraints: M0's db-open code must call `adapter.pragma('busy_timeout = ' + opts.timeout)` right after opening with node:sqlite, and should carry the same source-pin style test v1 used (tests/util/db-base-platform-gate.test.ts pattern: regex-assert the pragma call exists) so a future refactor cannot silently drop it again. Since 'no retry loop' is the ADR-0002 decision, correctness now depends entirely on busy_timeout being set correctly — there is no withRetry safety net this time.

docGapFinding.gap: Does not state that node:sqlite requires an explicit busy_timeout pragma call because the {timeout} constructor option is silently ignored; without this the measured '0 busy errors' result cannot be reproduced in v2.

answers.recommendation: Add the explicit pragma call as a stated requirement in ADR-0002, not left to implementation discretion, and keep a regression test for it since there is no retry loop to mask the failure this time.

answers.question: What is the exact git tag and branch flow for the first v2 release: does 'release' branch get its own tag, separate from 'v*-rc*' tags used for live E2E?
answers.answer: Yes, two separate tag families on two different branches. On `v2`: tag `v2.*` (or manual dispatch) triggers release.yml, and separately `v*-rc*` tags on `v2` trigger the live-e2e.yml job (§6.9, no cron, workflow_dispatch + push tags v*-rc*). On `release`: there is no tag pushed by CI at all for day-to-day work — release.yml's publish job commits to `release` with a `Source-Commit:` trailer and tags that commit `v2.x.y` (ADR-0013 publish job). So `release` does get the real version tag (v2.x.y), while `v*-rc*` tags live on `v2` purely to gate the live E2E harness before a release is cut. The owner runs `/release` once; `gh workflow run` then does the version bump, build, tag and publish in one CI run — the owner does not cut tags by hand except rc tags for testing.
answers.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0013-release-automation.md (Design: release.yml jobs plan/build/publish); docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md §6.9 (rc tags, no cron); docs/v2/adr/0011-release-and-v1-transition.md (Branches table, CI release job)

answers.question: Is 'main frozen' enforced only by convention, or does M0 need a branch-protection rule or CI check that blocks direct pushes to main?
answers.answer: Only by convention today. ADR-0011 explains why main stays frozen (v1 /ctx-upgrade compares package.json version and no-ops if unchanged), and ADR-0013's weekly.yml on main only checks that 'repo settings have not drifted' — it detects drift, it does not block a push. No GitHub branch-protection rule or required-status-check blocking direct pushes to main is named in any ADR, TECH-SPEC, or README. A search of .github/ in this worktree found no branch-protection config.
answers.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0011-release-and-v1-transition.md (Why main stays frozen); docs/v2/adr/0013-release-automation.md (weekly.yml: 'a check that repo settings have not drifted'); grep of .github/ found no protection rule

docGapFinding.gap: States the freeze as policy and a drift-detector exists, but no branch-protection rule or CI check actually blocks a direct push to main; one accidental merge can still break the v1 freeze the whole PRD depends on.

answers.recommendation: Add a GitHub branch-protection rule on main (required PR reviews or at minimum a required status check) now, not just a weekly drift report after the fact. Since issues/PRs are disabled on this repo, branch protection via required status checks (not required reviews, which need PRs) is the practical option — recommend requiring the ci.yml status check and restricting who can push to main, decided by the owner.
